# The Letter of Paul to the Ephesians

The title identifies the letter as Paul’s; this source house does not settle historical authorship or date. The verified object is the 23-page Ephesians reverse-interlinear PDF hosted by SBLGNT, with Greek, English and grammatical rows. The selected passage is 1:9–10 on PDF page2, printed p.972. Full edition and translation metadata remain to be collated; the file is identified by URL and local hash.

[Acquired witness](https://www.sblgnt.com/download/revint/70-Ephesians.pdf). Retrieved and selected text checked on 8 September 2026. Local SHA-256: `c8a46b30d2a7febb1608140360420b9d411f80033eb2567a64c6b5f2670c4651`.

The witness **sources** [the historical branch](../../../../etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and **qualifies** the historical comparison in its [whole-field](../../../../etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Taylor’s generated operation remains distinct from the historical proposition.

## Selected passages

<a id="ephesians-sbl-reverse-interlinear-q001"></a>
### q001 — Administration in the fullness of times

**Paraphrase:** Disclosure of the divine purpose leads into an administration of the fullness of times and the gathering of things in heaven and on earth in Christ. The arrangement has an explicitly temporal and Christological office. This passage does not claim that every economy necessarily restores all of its participants in the same way.

**Locator:** Ephesians 1:9–10; PDF page2, printed p.972.

**Verification:** embedded text read and selected passage identified; no exact quotation or full-work collation claim.
